The verdicts and the reasons below are unchanged.

No critical defect and no regression at critical or major severity against live 39.4.1 (04cdcd45). The candidate is live plus three commits that touch 8 source files (the Leblanc staging tables, one scene flag, the FFX-2 HUD's intent placement, one optional option of the shared intent card, two wiring lines); no src/battle, src/data, src/engine, src/audio, save, pose, sprite or build-config file changed, so the engine's output, the saves, the sound and every other chapter's data are live's. 35 browser runs, 0 console errors, 0 failed requests; real attacks landed in every act; the chain reaches the results screen (28 s).

The hotfix does what Bailey picked ("Old spacing, real sizes"). All 8 placements equal release 39.4's, measured in the 39.4 preview worker by the same procedure (largest difference 0.01 in x and 0 in z); the nearest fiend stands 192, 221, 169 px from the girls at 1600x900 (39.4 211, 230, 184; live's lane 137, 130, 114) and no fiend touches the command list (188, 288, 227 px; 169 px at 2000x1012; 127 px at 1280x720); the real sizes are kept (Ormi 1.935, Logos 2.119, Leblanc 1.763, Dr. Goon 1.849, Fem-Goon 1.690); the camera is the same pose within the idle sway; the 39.4.1 advisor cap is gone (maxHeight unset; card top 40 to 108 px under the nearest feet); the intent card covers no head at 1280x720, 1600x900 or 2000x1012 and overlaps no other HUD panel; the hidden chapter stands every fiend identically and its door still opens party prep with the save untouched.

Nothing else moved: FFX-2 Chapter IV and FFX Chapter I first menus equal live's (178 of 178 and 175 of 175 HUD boxes within 3 px), the same real attack (Tidus 153 on Mortiorchis on both), and the shared intent card is the same box, text, body cap and fade on both builds (Chapter IV by default, Chapter I opened with E).

The phone's Act I (live's own defect, F3942-01) is no worse than live and milder than it was: the worst fiend 81, 69, 69, 65, 71 percent inside the slice at the first menu on the candidate (8 s on: 88, 87, 82, 88, 100) against 70, 100, 78, 22, 29 on live (13, 100, 54, 55, 56); I rate it polish now (it was major when a goon stood entirely outside).

One thing the driver must settle before the deploy: this tree's git-ignored art folder carries Bailey's approved but unreleased title painting "The Echo" (release 39.5), so the artifact adds art/title/echo.webp, echo.json and one art/derived.json entry that no code here loads (F3943-03). Shipped inert it changes nothing a player sees; this report names exactly that artifact (bundle cUSnFK7q, artifactHash 3637f1f4...). If the two files are moved out first, the bundle name and the hash change and critic-clear refuses this report until both are re-recorded. [addendum] The driver shipped it inert (option (a)): the deployed artifact holds exactly the three added files, the removed bundle and the changed files this report names, plus the regenerated art index.

Disclosed (polish, none a regression at major severity): F3943-01 the folded intent card (Act I at 1600x900; every act at 1280x720; the price of keeping it off the heads: Bailey's yes or no), F3943-02 the phone strip grazing one head's top 5 to 7 px in two debug-route captures, F3942-01 the phone Act I edge, F3942-03 the fiends read 0.60 to 0.85 of the girls (his pick's price), F3942-05 Act III plate names (as live and 39.4), and F3943-03. addendum.why: node tools/critic-clear.mjs --report critic/reviews/a021787a-focused.json refused: "report artifact hash is not the deployed artifact". The report named the hash of the reviewer's own rebuild (3637f1f4...), the deploy shipped 713f2d21... with the same bundle name (cUSnFK7q). This addendum finds out why, and re-binds the review to the deployed artifact only because every difference is benign and outside the changed area.
addendum.verdict: RE-BOUND. The two artifacts differ in exactly one hashed file, art/manifest.json (the generated art index): its generatedAt stamp and one entry, "echo", in its title list. Every behavioural result of the focused review stands for the deployed artifact, with the same verdicts.

reviewerArtifact.recomputedFromDisk: tools/artifact-manifest.mjs build --dir dist-gate --no-decode after the deploy: 4539 files, 9671976233 bytes, the same hash (data/dist-gate-rehash-summary.json)

method: Both file lists (path, bytes, sha256) compared key by key: 4539 keys each, same keys, same order (critic/reviews/a021787a-focused-addendum/scripts/diff-manifests.mjs, data/manifest-diff-reviewer-vs-deployed.txt).
The repo's own tools/artifact-manifest.mjs diff of the two: added [], removed [], changed ["art/manifest.json"] (data/manifest-diff-reviewer-vs-deployed.json).

artifactHashOf (sorted path<TAB>sha256 lines, the manifest itself and .nojekyll left out) recomputed for both lists, and for the deployed list with only the reviewer's art/manifest.json entry swapped in: that gives 3637f1f4... exactly, so that one entry accounts for the whole gap (scripts/substitute-proof.mjs, data/hash-substitution-proof.txt).
The two art/manifest.json files diffed line by line: two hunks (data/art-manifest.json.diff). Every other top-level key is equal; title2x is ["keyart"] in both.

The reviewer's dist-gate re-hashed from disk after the deploy: still 3637f1f4... (nothing moved under the evidence). The live site serves art/manifest.json with the deployed sha256 (data/live-art-manifest-sha256.txt).
Every reader of the title list read in src (data/readers-of-the-title-list.txt).

differences.what: art/manifest.json: sha256 cdb17da1b4af56b0f8d6d0915b7c614c36c1533d0d28fa3bc54f5a5aac7f30c7 (100,392 bytes, the file live 39.4.1 serves) against 40c33654ace0bf5ffd7fb7aaf848f04814444c53a1f126fbd6988d4aed4a6338 (100,404 bytes). The only hashed file that differs, +12 bytes.
detail: "generatedAt": "2026-10-07T04:45:15.370Z" against "2026-10-09T00:44:33.622Z": the build stamp (same length). tools/gen/manifest.mjs rewrites the file, stamp included, only when the listing changed ("When the content (ignoring the timestamp) is unchanged the file is left alone"), so the stamp moved because of the next line.

"title": ["keyart"] against ["echo", "keyart"] (`    "echo",` and its line feed are the 12 bytes): the art index lists public/art/title/echo.png, which the tree holds. The deploy regenerates the index before it builds (tools/deploy-pages.mjs, "The art index has to be regenerated from whatever the fleet finished since the last release, before vite copies public/"; public/art/manifest.json was rewritten at 20:44 local, 19 minutes before the deploy). The reviewer's direct `vite build` (logs/vite-build.log of the focused evidence) does not run that step, so dist-gate carried the stale index of 2026-10-07, which did not yet list the plate.
differences.cause: the deploy's own regeneration of the art index; the echo plate was already in both artifacts (art/title/echo.webp, art/title/echo.json and the art/derived.json entry have the same sha256 in both manifests, and the bundle's embedded art list names art/title/echo.png in both: same bundle bytes). Disclosed as F3943-03.
whyBenign: The title list is read in two places only: judge() in src/engine/ArtManifest.ts, which answers manifestKnowsAsset/manifestKnowsAssetNow for the URL of a plate the caller asks about, and hasTitleArt(), which has no caller. The only title plate any source asks about is TITLE_PLATE = art/title/keyart.png (src/app/screens/frontend/titleMarkup.ts); the retina path reads title2x, which is ["keyart"] in both indexes. No file under src names title/echo. A new entry nobody asks about changes no answer.
generatedAt is parsed into a field of the manifest object (ArtManifest.ts) and read nowhere.

The changed area (Chapter VI staging, the intent card, the hidden chapter that reuses the room) loads no title plate; the focused report measured the code path of the deployed bundle, which is byte-identical (assets/index-cUSnFK7q.js, assets/index-Ta9GcVj0.css, index.html, workers: same sha256 in both manifests).

It adds nothing a player can reach that was not already reachable: art/title/echo.webp is already fetchable by URL in both artifacts (F3943-03, shipped inert as option (a)). Corroboration, not part of the proof: the live review of this build (critic/reviews/a021787a-live.json) ran 9 browser sessions on the live page with the deployed art index, 0 console errors in all of them and 0 requests for art/title/echo.* in the two real-key sessions that logged requests.
